questions.stem: What is produced during the incomplete combustion of a hydrocarbon fuel?

options.text: Carbon monoxide and/or carbon (soot), plus water
Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides only

questions.explanation: Incomplete combustion occurs when there is insufficient oxygen. Instead of producing CO₂, the carbon forms carbon monoxide (CO) and/or carbon (soot). Water is still produced. Carbon monoxide is particularly dangerous as it is a toxic, odourless gas.

questions.stem: Why is hydrogen described as a 'clean' fuel?

options.text: Because it is the lightest element
Because the only product of its combustion is water
Because it is cheap to produce
Because it is easy to store and transport

questions.explanation: Hydrogen is considered a clean fuel because when it burns, the only product is water: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. No carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, soot, or sulfur dioxide is produced, making it free from the pollutants associated with fossil fuels.
